title: A Passage for the Summit
premise: Silas Hartwell, estranged son of a disgraced archaeologist and a river-digger by trade, pulls a sealed chest from the floodwaters bearing the crest of Vessia, a nation erased from every map. The chest contains half of an expedition ledger pointing to the source of the River Ansel, where his father vanished twenty years ago, and both a collector's syndicate and the last descendants of Vessia will kill to reach it first. Forced to guide a ragged crew upstream through drowned villages, hostile gorges, and the syndicate's hunters, Silas discovers the 'forbidden source' is a living settlement his father helped hide, and that his own compass was the key all along. In the end Silas chooses to bury the source's secret rather than sell it, paying his debt with the truth of who he is, and finds in the river people the family his blood denied him.
about_author: Ines Zhou is a former river surveyor who spent six seasons mapping tributaries before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about water, borders, and the people who live in the gaps between maps.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas Hartwell dredges the flooded outskirts of Marrow Bend for salvage, dodging creditors and memories of his father's disgrace. When his net snags a lead-lined chest stamped with an unknown seal, he hides it instead of reporting it. POV: Silas. Beat: wary curiosity — the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Half-Truth
chapters.summary: Inside the chest: a torn expedition ledger in his father's handwriting, naming the source of the River Ansel. Silas recognizes the compass etched on its cover as identical to his own keepsake. A stranger asking about 'river iron' spooks him into fleeing town. POV: Silas. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Debt Called Odile
chapters.summary: Silas seeks out Odile Ferran, a smuggler who once owed his father her life, to barter passage upstream. She agrees only because the syndicate has put a price on anyone carrying Vessian artifacts. POV: Odile. Beat: reluctant alliance; found family's first uneasy seed.

chapters.title: The Collector's Men
chapters.summary: Syndicate agent Bram Voss interrogates Marrow Bend's salvagers and finds Silas's trail. Meanwhile Silas and Odile recruit Tuck, a teenage lockpick fleeing the same debt collectors as Silas. POV: alternating Silas/Voss. Beat: the hunt begins; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Drowned Steeple
chapters.summary: The crew passes a village swallowed by a reservoir, where frescoes depict the Vessian seal. An old ferrywoman recognizes the compass and warns them the river 'remembers what it was told to forget.' POV: Silas. Beat: wonder shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: Tuck's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tuck secretly photographs the ledger pages to sell to Voss as insurance against being abandoned. Odile catches him but says nothing yet, testing loyalty. POV: Tuck. Beat: betrayal planted; loneliness articulated.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: In a canyon wall carved with thousands of erased names, the crew is ambushed by Voss's hired boatmen. Silas's knowledge of currents saves them, but they lose their fuel stores. POV: Odile. Beat: first real cost; trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Half a Map
chapters.summary: Repairing at a floating market, Silas meets Sefa, a Vessian-descended herbalist who reveals the other half of the ledger exists — held by her people, guarded for generations. She joins them to keep it out of syndicate hands. POV: Silas. Beat: hope with strings attached.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Voss buys Tuck's photographs and learns the route ahead. He offers Tuck full pardon for betrayal at the source; Tuck, terrified of being disposable, doesn't refuse. POV: Voss. Beat: antagonist humanized, threat sharpened.

chapters.title: White Water
chapters.summary: A storm forces the crew through unnavigable rapids; the boat breaks apart and Odile nearly drowns. Silas drags her ashore, and she finally tells him how his father saved her — and why she never repaid it. POV: Odile. Beat: grief shared; bond cemented.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: At a fortified toll crossing, the crew must trade something precious to pass. Silas gives up his father's journal pages — keeping only the compass — a sacrifice that quietly devastates him. POV: Silas. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Sefa's Country
chapters.summary: Sefa leads them through hidden paths marked in Vessian script, revealing her people survived the erasure by becoming untraceable. She tests whether Silas is a treasure-hunter or something better. POV: Sefa. Beat: identity theme surfaces — can he be trusted with a nation?

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Snowbound and starving, the group argues about turning back. Tuck confesses the photographs; Odile nearly casts him out, but Silas argues that everyone here was bought or broken once. POV: Tuck. Beat: lowest ebb; forgiveness as choice.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Wake
chapters.summary: They find Voss's camp abandoned — with evidence he executed a local guide who refused to talk. The luxury of neutrality dies; the crew understands this is no longer salvage, it's war over memory. POV: Odile. Beat: moral stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Father's Footprints
chapters.summary: In a cave shelter, Silas finds tools and a dated message proving his father reached the source alive twenty years ago — and chose to stay. Rage and longing collide; the compass needle begins behaving strangely near the walls. POV: Silas. Beat: personal mystery inverted.

chapters.title: The Needle Turns
chapters.summary: Following the compass's pull, the crew crosses a ridge into a hidden valley where the river rises from beneath a living city — Vessia, unextinguished. Sentinels capture them before they can speak. POV: Silas. Beat: awe turned to captivity.

chapters.title: The Council of Kept Names
chapters.summary: Before Vessia's council, Silas presents the ledger half and the compass — which fits a socket in the council hall, proving his father designed the city's concealment. They reveal his father died defending it from the last syndicate expedition. POV: Silas. Beat: inheritance of purpose.

chapters.title: Voss at the Gate
chapters.summary: Voss, guided by Tuck's old photographs and a traitor sentinel, breaches the valley with armed men. Tuck redeems himself by sabotaging the syndicate's explosives, buying the city hours. POV: Tuck. Beat: redemption purchased at risk.

chapters.title: The Floodgate Choice
chapters.summary: To stop Voss, the council can open the ancient floodgates and drown the approach — destroying part of their own hidden world. Silas, who knows the river's moods best, must pilot the diversion channel alone. POV: Silas. Beat: climax — survival priced in sacrifice.

chapters.title: Where the River Is Born
chapters.summary: In the roaring diversion, Silas confronts Voss at the floodgate controls; the waters take Voss and nearly Silas, who is pulled out by Odile and Tuck. The valley holds, scarred but free. POV: Silas/Odile. Beat: catharsis; the debt paid in full.

chapters.title: Burying the Seal
chapters.summary: The council votes to remain hidden; Silas proposes sinking the chest and ledger back into the source so no map can ever claim them. He asks not for reward but for a place among them — and is given his father's old workshop. POV: Sefa. Beat: identity resolved by belonging.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Spring: Silas, Odile, and Tuck run the river down toward the ordinary world, carrying nothing salvable and everything that matters. Silas finally reads the last page of his father's recovered letter — addressed simply to 'my child, whoever you become.' POV: Silas. Beat: quiet, earned peace; found family afloat.
